materials: Franklin Spelling Ace electronic spell checker
Level 4 letter tiles: 2 sets of A through Z plus Vowel Y, CH, TH, CK, SH, WH, TCH
Unit tiles: ALL, ANG, ING, ONG, UNG, ANK, INK, ONK, UNK, OLL, OLD, OLT, OST, ILD, IND
objectives: Divide words with three letters between vowels using a 1-2 split.
Avoid splitting digraphs and units during syllable division.
Identify and divide compound words by pulling the two words apart.
Spell compound words as one word when the two smaller words refer to one thing.
Read and spell Lesson 7 word, phrase, sentence, and story material.

beats.label: Tutor overview
beats.do: Set out rubber bands, the electronic spell checker, the Level 4 tile set, Units, binder paper, pencil, word frame, and blank cards.
beats.note: Tutor-only overview: Lesson 7 teaches the third syllable-division rule. When three letters come between vowels, use a 1-2 split, but never split digraphs or Units. Compound words are divided by pulling the two small words apart.

beats.label: Review prior extra practice

say.text: Let's take a look at your extra practice page. Go ahead and read the words to me.

beats.do: Review Lesson 6 extra practice. If it was not completed at home, complete a prior extra-practice page now.

board.title: Lesson 6 Extra Practice Review
board.subtitle: Use one of the prior lesson pages if needed.
board.text: Review Lesson 6 Extra Practice before beginning Lesson 7.

recovery.trigger: Student cannot complete the prior extra practice accurately.
prompts: Repeat the prior lesson before teaching Lesson 7.

beats.label: Review earlier division rules

say.text: Before I show you a new way to divide a word into syllables, let's review the rules you already know.

beats.do: Build RELAX and ADMIT. Student reviews that one letter between vowels moves to the end first, and two letters between vowels split.

expect: One letter moves to the end first.

beats.label: Teach 1-2 split

say.text: Today, I'm going to show you what to do if there are three letters between the vowels. When there are three letters, most of the time you do a 1-2 split.

beats.do: Build CONFLICT. Student counts three letters between vowels and divides CON-FLICT with a 1-2 split.
beats.note: 1-2 split means the first consonant goes with the first syllable and the other two move to the end.

beats.label: Practice 1-2 split and prior rules

say.text: Divide the word, say it, and tell me why you divided it there.

beats.do: Build NOSTRIL, EXPRESS, and COMPLEX. Student divides with the 1-2 split and reviews schwa and Campus Confess when they appear.

expect: Express has two S's because the last syllable is accented.

beats.note: Partial rule: Three letters between vowels usually take a 1-2 split.

beats.label: Do not split units

say.text: The 1-2 split works most of the time. But you have to be careful of digraphs and Units.

beats.do: Build BANKRUPT and KINGDOM. Student sees that Units contain a vowel and are never split; the Unit goes one way and everything else goes the other way.
beats.note: Use KINGDOM to review closed-O schwa in the unaccented syllable.

beats.label: Do not split digraphs

say.text: You never split a digraph. A digraph makes just one sound, so you treat it like one sound.

beats.do: Build ETHNIC and ANTHEM. Student divides without splitting TH and explains the digraph exception. Review IC for /ik/ at the end of a multi-syllable word.

expect: /ik/ at the end of a multi-syllable word is IC.

beats.label: Introduce compound words

say.text: Sometimes words with three letters between the vowels are actually two small words run together.

beats.do: Build SHELLFISH. Let the student try a 1-2 split, then show that Shell and Fish are two small words. Teach that compound words are divided by pulling the two small words apart.

expect: Pull the two small words apart.

beats.note: In a compound word, each small word is spelled exactly as it is by itself. Shell keeps Floss-rule double L.

beats.label: Practice compound spelling

say.text: Divide the compound word and explain why the small word keeps its spelling.

beats.do: Build PILLBOX and LIPSTICK. Student divides compound words and explains Floss in pill and the ICK spelling in stick.

expect: Each part is spelled as if it were a word by itself.

beats.label: Identify compounds orally

say.text: Listen to each word I say, then tell me if it is a compound word.

beats.do: Say drumstick, express, crosswalk, and sandbox. Student identifies compounds and names the two words.

beats.label: One word or two

say.text: If the two small words together refer to one thing, then write them as one word.

beats.do: Build SANDBOX and SOFTBALL. Student explains why each is one word and divides SOFT-BALL. Review that BALL keeps Floss-rule double L because each small word keeps its spelling.

expect: One word because it means one thing.
Each small word keeps its spelling.

text: How do you divide a compound word?
If it isn't a compound word, what kind of split would you do for three letters?
What are the two things you never split?

expect: Pull apart the two small words.
Never split a digraph or a Unit.

board.title: Syllable Division Rule #3
board.text: 3 letters: check for a compound word. Otherwise use a 1-2 split, but do not split a digraph or Unit.

images.label: Lesson 7 Page 228: Syllable Division Rule #3

beats.label: Spell real words with tiles

say.text: The first word is pantry. Repeat that word. Tap each syllable, build each syllable, and read each syllable exactly as it looks.

beats.do: Dictate real words with tiles. Leave the Franklin Spelling Ace within reach for uncertain spellings.
beats.note: Words: pantry, hundred, subtract, crosswind, handball, checklist. Repeat-lesson words: contract, simply, tantrum, inspect, nonstop. In compound words, each syllable is accented equally.

beats.label: Read nonsense words on tiles

say.text: Divide that word into syllables. Say each syllable exactly as it looks. Now say it like a word.

beats.do: Build nonsense words for the student to divide and read.
beats.note: Words: IXTRACT (in-TRACT), ROMSTON (ROM-stun), PANPRESS (pan-PRESS), LANDCAP (LAND-CAP), STRONGPIT (STRONG-PIT), DISHNICK (DISH-NICK). Repeat-lesson words: ENTRUM, DASTRO, HANDREST, HOPSTAFF, TRAMPLING.

beats.label: Spell nonsense words with tiles

say.text: Now it's your turn to spell nonsense words. Repeat the word, tap each syllable, and build each syllable.

beats.do: Dictate nonsense words with tiles, then move tiles out of the way.
beats.note: Words: EX-grit, san-PRESS, WIN-fict, OFF-RAG (compound), DUST-CUFF (compound), CHECK-LOCK (compound). Repeat-lesson words: PAN-grip, EX-maft, con-TRESS, UP-TRICK (compound), TRAM-NET (compound). Sanpress has two S's because the last syllable lasts the longest.

beats.label: Read words through word frame

say.text: Now you're going to read words through the word frame. If you don't know the word, use your pencil to help you divide it.

beats.do: Student reads the Lesson 7 word page through the word frame. Optional: circle each compound word.

beats.label: Spell words on paper

say.text: Now you'll spell on paper, syllable by syllable. If you hear a schwa and aren't absolutely sure which vowel changed, use your electronic spell checker.

beats.do: Dictate real and nonsense words on paper.
beats.note: Real words: extract, withhold, constant, saffron, handbag. Nonsense words: PUFF-GUN (compound), ex-FLICT, DROP-TRAP (compound), IN-stim. Repeat real words: SMALL-POX, impress, camshaft, freshman, mongrel. Repeat nonsense: ex-PLANT, TRACK-PIN, ETH-rip, MON-step, com-DRAFT.

beats.label: Review sight word reading deck

say.text: Let's review your Sight Word Reading Deck. Warm up by reading each card, then keep the clue hidden and read them again as fast as you can.

beats.do: Use the student's physical Sight Word Reading Deck. Skip if unavailable.

beats.label: Review sight word spelling cards

say.text: Let's review your tricky sight words.

beats.do: For each physical Sight Word Spelling Card: read, explain the red letter, see and spell twice on the wall, see and write twice on the table, and see and write twice on paper. Dictate active sight words later after phrase spelling.
beats.note: Retire a card after three correct sessions and replace it from the Sight Word Check List.

beats.label: Read phrases

say.text: Now you'll read some phrases. Create sentences, then point to two compound words.

beats.do: Student reads phrase groups, creates sentences, and identifies two compound words.

beats.label: Spell phrases on paper

say.text: Now you're going to write some phrases. Repeat the phrase, write it down, and figure out the tough words syllable by syllable.

beats.do: Dictate phrases, then dictate the three active sight words from the spelling deck.
beats.note: Phrases: CAMSHAFT IS BROKEN; FILTHY KITTEN. Repeat-lesson phrases: CONTRACT SMALLPOX; HIS MUSKRAT; IN AN INSTANT.

beats.label: Read sentences

say.text: Read that first sentence to yourself. Now read it out loud. Mark each phrase, then reread with phrasing.

beats.do: Student reads, marks phrases, rereads with phrasing, and optionally circles compound words.

board.title: Lesson 7 Read These Sentences
items: The hungry bulldog began to yap in the kitchen by the sandwich.
My grandson had a tantrum behind the pantry but I didn't spank him.
Mr. Kingston went bankrupt in Richmond so no one would know.
Their children will install a sickbed in the attic for Alfred.
His offhand comment did not impress me.
My mattress is filthy and much too soft.
Mr. Jackson will inspect the blacktop.
Winston is such a contrast to the rest of her children.

beats.label: Spell sentences on paper

say.text: Now you're going to write three sentences. Repeat the sentence, write it, tap the syllables on long words, and check your sentence.

beats.do: Dictate three sentences and guide correction.
beats.note: Sentences: MY CAMSHAFT AND DIPSTICK ARE BROKEN. PUT THE FILTHY KITTEN IN THE BATHTUB. WILL YOU PUT A BLINDFOLD ON MR. WINSTON? Repeat-lesson sentences: MY GRANDSON DID CONTRACT SMALLPOX. HIS MUSKRAT IS IN THE ATTIC. IN AN INSTANT, THE BANDIT DID CONFESS.

beats.label: Read basic stories

say.text: Now you're ready to read a story. Preread the story and figure out the tough words. Then read it out loud to me.

beats.do: Have the student read the first story aloud. For the second story, have the student read silently and retell in their own words.

board.title: Lesson 7 Stories - Basic

stories.title: Mrs. Hudson
stories.text:
Mrs. Hudson does spend a lot of cash to stock her pantry.

If she has a hint that you are hungry, she'll rush to the kitchen and put on her cotton apron. She'll fix a batch of lemon strudel and pop it in the oven.

The kitchen is her kingdom, and all of her stuff is yummy. If you are a friend of Mrs. Hudson, you could get fat.

stories.title: The Handbag
stories.text:
Bonny can't find her lipstick. She is sure that it must be in her handbag.

She did find a pencil she had lost and an old traffic ticket. She did find a bran muffin and some chopsticks.

Alfred told her there was too much junk in her handbag. He said she should get a backpack.

Do you think that would help?

board.text: Read Story #1 aloud. Read Story #2 silently and retell.

beats.label: Read advanced stories
beats.do: Use these instead of the basic stories when appropriate for the student.

stories.title: Mr. Cranston
stories.text:
Mr. Cranston couldn't suppress a grin. The children were busy smuggling a straggly mongrel into the pantry.

His instinct told him he should confront the kids and banish the mutt. But his giggly children did enchant him, and Mr. Cranston doesn't do well with conflict.

It is a complex task to be both a father and a friend.

stories.title: Lucky Jason
stories.text:
Jason had a black belt in Judo. He won a windfall at Blackjack in Reno. He was a whiz in the cockpit. He was also a kingpin in Congress.

To put it simply, Jason was a success.

So it was a shock when he had a sudden crackup and became a rambling windbag.

beats.label: Wrap up

say.text: You've done a lot of reading and spelling today. Thank you for working so hard.

beats.do: Assign optional extra practice only if the student asks for between-session practice. Always do the first problem together before sending a page home.

board.title: Lesson 7 Extra Practice
board.subtitle: Rendered from the real Book 4 manual pages before Lesson 8
board.text: Show Lesson 7 Extra Practice #1 or #2. The student completes the selected paper copy outside the app.

beats.note: Extra Practice #1 asks the student to divide real words and mark each vowel sound as Short, Long, Schwa, or a Unit. Extra Practice #2 asks the student to form compound words by drawing lines between columns.
